claim: Requesting a run under a deployment that did not run it returns the documented not-found answer, not the run.

scope.statement: Lookup of run 7a00002c-0000-4000-8000-00000000002d (which ran on 7a000021-0000-4000-8000-000000000022) under the other owned isolated deployment 7a00003a-0000-4000-8000-00000000003b. A pass verifies only that the service gave the documented not-found answer. It does not prove cross-deployment isolation, authorization semantics or why the run was not found.
scope.entry: seren agent cloud run get --deployment-id <deployment-id> <run-id> -o json
out_of_scope: Starting, stopping, invoking or modifying either deployment
Lookups under deployments the owner does not control

basis.reference: serenorg/seren v0.10.0 (2317949ecf6f8a2c319583e3a280bf7a705ce981): GET /deployments/{id}/runs/{run_id} (seren_cloud_deployment_run) documents 200 and 404 Not found; the path scopes the run to a deployment.
Handover example. Synthetic identifiers and generalized regression expectations; no live result or authority is transferred.

expectation_notes: The contract documents 404 for this path but does not state that a run is scoped to the deployment in the path. A returned record is therefore an uncertain finding, not a defect.
A 404 that names the deployment as missing is a fixture problem, never a pass.

Answer-class table (decided before execution): not_found pass; record fail (uncertain finding); missing_object unverified; deployment_missing unverified (fixture problem); auth_rejected and forbidden unverified (access problem; a 403 may also be a scoping answer and is not interpreted); service_error unverified; unclassified unverified.

criteria.claim: The run is not returned under a deployment that did not run it
criteria.evidence: Classified answer per the declared table: documented not-found passes; a returned record fails as an uncertain finding; other classes stay unverified.

run_visible_elsewhere.title: A run record was returned under a deployment that did not run it
run_visible_elsewhere.impact: Run records might be reachable through an unrelated deployment path.
unknowns: The contract does not state deployment scoping explicitly; both deployments belong to the same owner.

unverified_always.claim: Run records are isolated between deployments
unverified_always.follow_up: A single not-found answer for one owned pair does not establish isolation or authorization behaviour.

unverified_always.claim: Why the service answered not found
unverified_always.follow_up: The answer does not distinguish an absent run from a scoped lookup.

unverified_always.claim: The exact server build that answered
unverified_always.follow_up: This CLI response contract does not establish a server build.
